# Original Vial 0.7.5 codec fixture

These files are unmodified upstream sources. They let `python3 tests/vial_codec_roundtrip.py` exercise the actual Vial serialization and deserialization logic offline with the standard Python runtime. They are test fixtures, never imported by the runtime comparison tool. No Qt stub or GUI dependency is needed.

Vial GUI v0.7.5 resolves to commit `e42622c352b69eff523a467718db487ab9c9cbf2`. The original files are `src/main/python/keycodes/keycodes.py`, `keycodes_v5.py`, `keycodes_v6.py` and `src/main/python/any_keycode.py`. The empty `keycodes/__init__.py` is only a local package marker. Both original protocol tables are retained because the original codec imports both. Vial's GPL-2.0-or-later notice and complete original `COPYING` are retained.

The original Vial `requirements.txt` pins simpleeval at commit `41c99b8e224a7a0ae0ac59c773598fe79a4470db`. Its original `simpleeval.py` and MIT `LICENCE`, stored here as `simpleeval-LICENCE`, are included. [provenance.json](provenance.json) records each upstream path and SHA256. The test checks every hash before reporting success. Upstream sources are [Vial GUI](https://github.com/vial-kb/vial-gui/tree/e42622c352b69eff523a467718db487ab9c9cbf2) and [simpleeval](https://github.com/danthedeckie/simpleeval/tree/41c99b8e224a7a0ae0ac59c773598fe79a4470db).

The test calls `recreate_keyboard_keycodes` with protocol6, the source's layer/macro/Tap Dance counts, and no custom metadata, matching this repository's `vial.json`. It runs original `deserialize`, `serialize` and re-deserialization for every one of the 896 layout cells and 128 encoder cells in each document. Physical holes are also checked numerically through the codec. The simulated export retains their integer `-1` sentinel, as original `src/main/python/protocol/keyboard_comm.py` `save_layout` does for missing physical coordinates; they are never writable bindings.

Stock Vial registers only `USER00` through `USER15` without `customKeycodes`. The canonical source and logical trial each have eight Picker15 cells containing `USER16` through `USER19`. The regression proves their original `deserialize(..., reraise=True)` failures and silent-zero default. It separately reads their numeric identity with original `Keycode.resolve`, which uses the intact protocol6 table, and proves the codec exports and accepts `0x7e10` through `0x7e13`. It never registers invented custom metadata to hide the problem.

For the full successful source and trial roundtrips, only those eight spellings are replaced before import. Every other cell uses the original codec directly. The test derives the complete observed alias table from both exported documents and requires exact equality with the runtime tool's small table. No generic expression or hexadecimal parser is added to that tool. Wrong chords, unexpected strings, changed data and lost Picker bindings remain drift.

The separate legacy-source test also imports every original source cell with the original default `deserialize` behavior. It proves that the complete lossy export matches only the separately named exact legacy-source profile, with all eight affected Picker cells equal to `KC_NO`. This profile is not source equivalence. All 254 possible nonempty partial-loss subsets are rejected by the asset tests, along with wrong-cell loss and extra edits.
